# E8 QUARANTINE: every fit, threshold and selection in this file is made on E3-E7 only; E8 rows are ONE labeled blind read and were never an input to any choice.

# WHY PREV-ERA TRANSFERS AND THE INNER BLOCK DOES NOT.  My first guess was a slow regime variable.  The fold arithmetic says something simpler and worse: `newobj_arms.fold` splits the TRAINING block by day, so the inner validation days come from the same prior eras the previous-era selector uses — they are nearly the same DAYS.  What differs is the SCORE.  The folded champion column FOLD_<era>_<seed>.npy is trained on the WHOLE training block and the inner validation days are INSIDE it.

# So S_XGB is OUT-OF-SAMPLE on the eval era and IN-SAMPLE on the inner block.  The inner-block selector was never valid for the one column that wins, and the 'disagreement' is not evidence against the arm — it is a defect in the selector.
# The spearman columns are the test: a materially HIGHER score-to-certificate rank correlation on the inner block than on the eval era is the in-sample signature.
